links.targetTitle: The Root Edit Primitive is non-operational until a Prime Age
Approved Root Edits are executed by the Operational Facilita

title: A Prime Agent never edits its own Artifact — token holders vote and the Operational Executor Agent actions the edit
content:
A.2.2.6.2 defines the Root Edit Primitive as allowing Prime Agents "through a token holder vote, to direct the Operational Executor Agent specified in the Executor Accord Primitive to **directly modify** the Prime Agent Artifact." The Agent's own governance produces an instruction; a third party carries it out.

A.2.2.6.2.2.2 makes the four conditions non-negotiable regardless of how an Agent designs the rest of its process: "(1) Agent token holders must vote to approve Artifact Edit proposals, (2) the Operational Facilitator must review each proposal for alignment and conformance with the process specified in the Root Edit Primitive, (3) the vote must be conducted by the Operational Facilitator, and (4) the Operational Facilitator must action the Artifact Edit if the vote passes."

The operational sequence in A.2.2.6.2.1.2.1–4 shows the checks in order: proposal, Facilitator review on two axes (alignment with the Atlas, and compliance with the Agent's own stated requirements), Facilitator-run vote, then Facilitator actions the edit in Powerhouse and records the outcome and materials either way.

Two properties follow. First, alignment review is unavoidable — there is no path by which an Agent's holders can enact an Atlas-misaligned edit, because the party who executes edits is also the party who screens them. Second, condition (4) is a genuine obligation on the Facilitator, not just a permission: a passed vote must be actioned, which stops the reviewer from becoming a silent veto after the fact.
description: Root Edit's four mandatory conditions place proposal review, vote administration, and execution with the Operational Facilitator, so no Agent can amend itself directly.
